questions.stem: What is the time complexity of accessing an element in a dynamic array?
questions.explanation: Accessing an element in a dynamic array is $O(1)$ because each element can be directly accessed via its index. This is due to the contiguous memory allocation of arrays, which allows for constant time computation of the memory address of any element. The most tempting wrong option might be $O(n)$, but this would imply that accessing an element requires traversing the array, which is not the case.

questions.stem: What is the time complexity of inserting an element at the beginning of a dynamic array?
questions.explanation: Inserting an element at the beginning of a dynamic array is $O(n)$ because it requires shifting all existing elements one position to the right to make space for the new element. This shifting operation takes linear time relative to the number of elements in the array. The option $O(1)$ might seem appealing, but it ignores the need to move elements.

questions.stem: What is the main advantage of using dynamic arrays over static arrays?
questions.explanation: The main advantage of dynamic arrays over static arrays is automatic resizing. Dynamic arrays can grow or shrink in size as needed, which is managed by allocating a larger array and copying elements when the current capacity is exceeded. This flexibility is not present in static arrays, which have a fixed size. Faster access time is not an advantage over static arrays, as both have $O(1)$ access time.
